sources.full: Trouble at Grog's — Hall Qualification Conversion

contents.name: Chapter 3: Return to the Happy Orc
Appendix A: Clues and Failure Modes

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: Three-hour Hall one-shot for four or five 3rd-level PCs.
Run three investigation beats, then the finale at the Happy Orc. Clues fail forward.
Assume the PCs arrive at the finale near full strength and will spend every resource.
Named cast only: Grog, Yuri Kinnon, Sid Barrow, Grunt, Jim Ramsey, Ellie Felan.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Grog is an orc retired adventurer whose Happy Orc tavern is highly successful.

Yuri Kinnon owns the competing Dagger Rock Tavern and wants Grog ruined. Grunt burns a stable, Jim falsely claims an orc fled, and Ellie steals/plants evidence at the Happy Orc. Yuri coordinates all three.
Sid Barrow is Grog's honest friend in local law enforcement and needs evidence before acting.

entries.name: The Conspiracy

entries.caption: Frame-Up
rows: Supplies the false orc eyewitness story.

entries: The stable is not connected to Grog except through the manufactured accusation.
Two independent Yuri links, or one strong link plus decisive physical evidence, are enough.

entries.name: Maps
entries: Keep the Happy Orc main-floor map on the table all session. Stable/Yard and Tunnel Chamber are optional only.

entries.name: Opening
entries: The Happy Orc is loud, cheap, generous, rowdy, successful, and welcoming. Grog looks intimidating but is immediately friendly.
Grog says recent crimes are increasingly blamed on orcs and people associated with his tavern. He believes someone is framing him and asks the outsider PCs to investigate.
If the PCs distrust Grog, let them investigate him. They find ordinary flaws, not organized-crime evidence.

entries.caption: Leads
rows: False eyewitness account and possible Yuri contact.
Planted evidence or covert access if they search deeply.

entries.name: Running the Investigation
entries: Run three substantive beats unless the players solve it sooner.
Use DC 12 cooperative, 14 guarded, 16 frightened/subtle. Do not roll when the method logically works.
A failed check costs time, creates suspicion, gives incomplete information, or alerts Yuri; it never deletes the only path forward.

entries.name: Stable Fire
entries: The stable is elsewhere in town and is not Grog's property. Accelerant, tampering, tracks, witnesses, magic, or animals can show the fire was deliberate and point toward Grunt.
Jim claims he saw an orc flee. The scene and timeline give the PCs ways to challenge that claim.

entries.name: Grunt
entries: Grunt may tail or intimidate before fighting. If captured or cornered, he identifies Yuri as his employer for the arson/intimidation work.
Use {@creature thug|MM}. He is not suicidal. If neutralized here, he is absent from the finale and is not replaced.

entries.name: Jim Ramsey
entries: Jim repeats the same anti-Grog stories with suspicious consistency. His key claim is that he saw an orc flee the stable.
Comparison with the scene, surveillance, pressure, or magic can crack the story. Following him can expose a Yuri-linked payment/contact.

entries.name: Ellie Felan
entries: Ellie is Yuri's theft/evidence specialist and only named lieutenant. She steals property and uses hidden access, disguise, timing, or magic to plant evidence at the Happy Orc.
Catching her with stolen goods or matching a cache to Sid's inventory can become decisive evidence. If exposed, she tries to move or destroy evidence on-screen and warns Yuri if able.

entries.name: Sid Barrow
entries: Sid has a stolen-property inventory and notes separating verified facts from rumors. He corroborates; he does not announce the solution.
If the PCs are stuck, he can identify a stolen item linked to Yuri's sphere or show that Jim's timeline conflicts with verified facts.

entries.name: Yuri Kinnon
entries: Yuri is composed in public. Routine questions make him appear cooperative while he alerts his people. Direct accusation without proof accelerates the endgame.
The finale triggers when player success threatens the scheme, not because a timer expires.

entries.caption: Evidence
rows: Sid treats Yuri as a formal suspect.

data.name: Chapter 3: Return to the Happy Orc

entries.name: Maps
entries: The Happy Orc main floor is the finale map. Optional yard/tunnel zones only if the fight actually moves there.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: Once Yuri knows the scheme is collapsing, he makes one last move at the Happy Orc to preserve or destroy the planted evidence and break the people who exposed him.
The place where the PCs met Grog becomes the place they save.

entries.name: Enemy Roles
entries: Yuri is physically present and is the boss. Ellie controls space and protects/moves evidence. Grunt appears only if not already neutralized. Unnamed bandits provide extra bodies. Jim is not a default combatant.

entries.name: Running the Fight

entries.caption: Enemy Plan
rows: Yuri attacks a dangerous PC; Ellie controls/conceals; muscle spreads out and blocks lanes.
Yuri presses the strongest threat; Ellie moves/protects evidence; muscle collapses on isolated PCs.
Bloodied Yuri becomes more aggressive and fights until dropped; Ellie/muscle may flee or surrender once the fight is decided.

entries: Yuri does not flee or surrender simply because he is losing. At 0 HP he dies unless the players deliberately take him alive with a legal nonlethal melee attack.
Do not repeatedly attack unconscious PCs while conscious threats remain.

entries.name: Objectives
entries: Defeat Yuri, keep the Happy Orc from being framed, protect civilians, secure evidence, and stop Ellie from destroying or escaping with it.
Grog protects patrons/staff. Sid contains the scene and handles survivors. Neither is default allied DPR.
Good investigation changes starting position, evidence control, and whether Grunt is present; it does not remove the climax.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: If Yuri dies and enough evidence survives, Sid clears Grog and arrests surviving conspirators.
If Ellie escapes with some evidence, other testimony plus Yuri's public violence can still clear Grog if the PCs built a credible case.
If the PCs deliberately take Yuri alive, Sid arrests him.
End at the Happy Orc, not in a council chamber.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: Primary reward: Grog's name is cleared and the Happy Orc survives.
Grog pays any fee established at the opening; otherwise use the Hall's normal one-shot convention.
Recovered stolen property belongs to its owners. Grog offers food, drink, lodging, and permanent welcome.

data.name: Appendix A: Clues and Failure Modes

entries.caption: Redundant Clues
rows: Deliberate fire; Jim's false story; planted property.
Physical evidence; tracks; magic; surveillance; confession.
Timeline; scene evidence; surveillance; magic; pressure.
Stolen-goods match; surveillance; caught possession; hidden-route use.
Grunt employer link; Jim payment/contact; Ellie connection; Yuri's reactions.

entries.name: Unexpected Approaches
entries: Let Zone of Truth, Detect Thoughts, Speak with Animals, surveillance, capture, and early tunnel discovery work normally. Successful magic or clever play may shorten the mystery; Yuri simply reacts sooner.
If the players solve the case early, go to the finale. Do not invent more mystery.
Never destroy an essential clue on one failed check.

entries.name: Finale Scaling — Level 3

entries.caption: Happy Orc Finale
rows: Yuri Kinnon; Ellie Felan; Grunt if available; 3 unnamed {@creature bandit|MM}s
Yuri Kinnon; Ellie Felan; Grunt if available; 4 unnamed {@creature bandit|MM}s

entries: Assume a full one-shot nova. Yuri is deliberately tougher than a Bandit Captain so he survives the opening burst.
If Grunt was neutralized earlier, remove him and do not replace him.

entries.name: Resource Check
entries: Target a hard climax: major resources spent, one or more PCs may hit 0 HP, and Yuri survives long enough to matter.
Control lethality with targeting, terrain, Ellie's spell choices, and hired-muscle surrender rather than secretly reducing Yuri's hit points.

entries.name: One-Page Running Reference
entries: 4–5 level-3 PCs; three-hour target; three investigation beats.
Named cast only: Grog, Yuri, Sid, Grunt, Jim, Ellie.
Truth: Yuri is mastermind; Grunt burns stable; Jim lies that an orc fled; Ellie steals/plants evidence; Grog is innocent; Sid is ally.
Stable is not Grog's property.
Two independent Yuri links or decisive planted evidence is enough.
Finale: Happy Orc. Yuri + Ellie + Grunt if available + unnamed bandits.
Yuri: AC 16, 95 HP, three attacks, Dirty Fighting, Parry, bloodied counterattack. Yuri fights to 0 HP unless deliberately taken alive.
Grog protects civilians; Sid secures scene. Neutralized Grunt stays gone.

trait.name: Cunning Action
entries: Yuri can Dash or Disengage as a bonus action.

trait.name: Dirty Fighting (1/Turn)
entries: Yuri deals an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage on a weapon hit when he has advantage or an active ally is within 5 feet of the target.

trait.name: Last Stand
entries: At 47 hit points or fewer, Yuri fights until reduced to 0 hit points unless deliberately incapacitated nonlethally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Yuri makes three weapon attacks.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) piercing damage.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d4 + 4}) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: Yuri adds 3 AC against one melee attack that would hit him; he must see the attacker and wield a melee weapon.

reaction.name: Desperate Counterattack
entries: At 47 hit points or fewer, when a creature within 5 feet misses him with an attack, Yuri can make one Shortsword attack against it.
